1→# Floodplain & Waterway Protection Feasibility — Austin, TX
     2→
     3→## Domain
     4→
     5→Austin's FWP discipline encompasses three overlapping regulatory regimes that any waterway-adjacent or low-lying parcel must navigate: (1) federal FEMA SFHA / FIRM compliance, (2) the City of Austin's **stricter** fully-developed-conditions floodplain (with Atlas 14 rainfall data in updated watersheds), and (3) the environmental buffer system — Critical Water Quality Zone (CWQZ), Water Quality Transition Zone (WQTZ), Erosion Hazard Zone (EHZ), and Critical Environmental Feature (CEF) buffers — that surrounds classified waterways. Also in scope: floodplain modification analysis, no-rise certification for the COA floodway, finished floor elevation / freeboard, ASCE 24 structural compliance, watershed impervious cover limits, and the variance pathways (administrative, LUC, Council) that unlock relief.
     6→
     7→Bridges to other disciplines: CWQZ overlaps with `el` (Environmental Landscape); impervious cover and water quality treatment overlap with `sde` (Site Drainage & Environmental); building elevations and FFE overlap with `sduf` (Site Development & Utilities Framework).
     8→
     9→## Authoritative sources
    10→
    11→- **FEMA FIRM panels** — current effective panels via msc.fema.gov; preliminary FIRMs if a watershed restudy is in progress
    12→- **COA fully-developed 100-year floodplain** — derived from approved City regulatory hydraulic models intersected with site-specific topo (DCM 1.2.6.B); shown on COA GIS layer alongside FEMA
    13→- **COA 25-year floodplain (= COA floodway)** — Atlas 14 areas: 25-yr fully developed; non-Atlas 14 areas: 100-yr fully developed pre-Atlas 14 (LDC § 25-12-52(11))
    14→- **Land Development Code (LDC) Chapter 25-7** — Drainage / floodplain regulation (definitions § 25-7-2; calculation methods § 25-7-6; encroachment variances § 25-7-92; exceptions §§ 25-7-93, 25-7-95, 25-7-96; easement requirements § 25-7-152)
    15→- **Land Development Code (LDC) Chapter 25-8** — Water Quality (CWQZ § 25-8-261; floodplain modification § 25-8-263; CWQZ uses § 25-8-281; cut/fill §§ 25-8-341 / 25-8-342; interbasin diversion § 25-8-365; admin variances § 25-8-42; LUC variances § 25-8-41)
    16→- **LDC Chapter 25-12** — Floodplain administration (design flood elevation § 25-12-52; FFE / freeboard / floodproofing § 25-12-53; floodway no-rise / encroachment variances § 25-12-54)
    17→- **Drainage Criteria Manual (DCM)** — Floodplain delineation methodology (§ 1.2.6); hydraulic study requirements (§§ 1.2.4–1.2.5); EHZ analysis procedure (Appendix E); Atlas 14 / TP40-TP49 (§ 2.3.1); dam safety (§ 8.3.3.B); culvert headwater limits (§ 1.2.4.C/D)
    18→- **Environmental Criteria Manual (ECM)** — Floodplain modification criteria (§ 1.7); FAFH (§ 1.7.4 + App. X); restoration ratios (§ 1.7.5); CWQZ buffer averaging (§ 1.5.2.D); EARZ basin liners (§ 1.6.2.C); CEF setbacks (§ 1.10); admin variance form (§ 1.3.3)
    19→- **Rule R161-20.01** — Atlas 14 compliance (effective 2019-11-25)
    20→- **ASCE 24-14** — Flood Resistant Design and Construction (referenced by LDC § 25-12-53)
    21→- **Property records** — recorded drainage easements, plat notes, prior CLOMR/LOMR documentation, prior variance approvals
    22→
    23→## Regulatory pathway
    24→
    25→| Pathway | Decision body | Typical timeline | When triggered |
    26→|---|---|---|---|
    27→| Floodplain Development Permit | WPD / DSD floodplain administrator | concurrent with site plan | Any development in or affecting the 100-yr or 25-yr floodplain |
    28→| CLOMC / CLOMR (FEMA) | FEMA + COA acknowledgment | 6–12 months for review; CLOMC acknowledgment required **before preliminary plan or site plan permit** | Pre-construction map revision (e.g. fill, channel work that alters FEMA SFHA) |
    29→| LOMR (FEMA) | FEMA | 6–12 months; final acceptance required **before CO** | Post-construction map revision |
    30→| Administrative environmental variance (LDC § 25-8-42) | WPD Director, no hearing | weeks; ECM 1.3.3 form required | Enumerated items only: cut/fill 4–8 ft in DDZ, CEF buffer reduction, interbasin diversion below threshold, etc. |
    31→| LUC environmental variance (LDC § 25-8-41) | Land Use Commission after Environmental Commission recommendation | 3–6 months | Cut/fill >8 ft, cut/fill in DWPZ, CWQZ encroachment, floodplain modification with adverse impact, slopes >15%, within 100 ft of classified waterway |
    32→| Floodplain encroachment variance (LDC § 25-7-92) | Council (or LUC under some scenarios) | 6+ months | Buildings or parking in 25-yr or 100-yr floodplain not covered by §§ 25-7-93 / 25-7-96 exceptions |
    33→| Floodway encroachment variance (LDC § 25-12-54) | Council | 6+ months; **cannot be granted if any flood-level rise results** (§ 25-12-54(F)(5)) | Any work in COA 25-yr floodplain (floodway) with rise |
    34→| Save Our Springs (Article 13) | **No variance available** | — | Any project in the Barton Springs Zone — SOS is inviolable |
    35→
    36→Project file must show CLOMC acknowledgment letter from FEMA **before** preliminary plan / site plan permit issues; LOMC acknowledgment **before** final acceptance / BP; LOMR final acceptance **before** CO.
    37→
    38→## Constraints to evaluate
    39→
    40→### Mapping & delineation
    41→
    42→- **Two floodplains, not one.** Always map both the FEMA SFHA (copy directly from current FIRM shapefile per DCM 1.2.6.B — do not re-delineate to onsite topo) and the COA fully-developed 100-yr floodplain (derived from approved City hydraulic models intersected with site topo). For pre-feasibility, assume the COA boundary is larger than FEMA wherever Atlas 14 has been applied.
    43→- **Hydraulic study trigger:** any creek, channel, or area of concentrated flow with ≥64 acres contributing drainage area requires a COA floodplain delineation (DCM 1.2.6.A.1). Below 64 acres, no COA floodplain is defined unless City or FEMA already mapped it.
    44→- **Preliminary FIRM in process?** Check whether the watershed has a pending FEMA restudy. Using an effective FIRM when a preliminary is published is a common deficiency.
    45→
    46→### Floodway (COA 25-yr) — the hardest constraint
    47→
    48→- **0.00-ft rise standard.** Any encroachment in the COA 25-yr floodplain requires PE-certified zero rise, delivered as a **separate** sealed letter (LDC § 25-12-54(D)(11)) — not just the WSE comparison table.
    49→- **Council cannot grant variance for floodway encroachment if any rise would result** (LDC § 25-12-54(F)(5)). Buildings, parking, or fill in the floodway with rise are categorically infeasible — design must avoid the floodway.
    50→
    51→### 100-yr floodplain — buildings & parking
    52→
    53→- Buildings and parking are prohibited in both 25-yr and 100-yr floodplains absent an enumerated exception (§ 25-7-93 for 100-yr; § 25-7-96 for 25-yr) or a Council encroachment variance (§ 25-7-92(C)) finding all seven criteria.
    54→- **§ 25-7-93 exception conditions:** ≥2 ft above 100-yr WSE, volume compensation (compensatory storage), no additional adverse impact. Five enumerated categories (e.g. parking <5,000 sq ft with director "no adverse effect" determination).
    55→- **Finished floor elevation:** minimum 2-ft freeboard above design flood elevation (LDC § 25-12-53(C)(1)). Design flood elevation = higher of Atlas 14 100-yr or FEMA 500-yr WSEL.
    56→- **Safe access:** building access at or above 1 ft above DFE, equivalent to the Regulatory Flood Datum (LDC § 25-12-53(C)(4)(a)).
    57→- **ASCE 24-14 certification** required for structures in the floodplain — separate engineer-sealed letter per structure type (retaining walls, fill, culverts, bridges, piers, fencing, buildings).
    58→- **Below-grade structures, MEP equipment elevation, flood openings for enclosed areas, safe refuge space** — all separately addressed by LDC § 25-12-53.
    59→- **Post-construction elevation certificate** (FEMA Form 086-0-33) by licensed surveyor — required prior to CO.
    60→
    61→### Floodplain modification
    62→
    63→- Any fill, grading, or channel work in the regulatory floodplain triggers LDC § 25-8-263 modification analysis: no-rise WSE, no increase in downstream peak flows, no loss of floodplain storage. WSE comparison table for 2/10/25/100-yr storms required.
    64→- **Functional Assessment of Floodplain Health (FAFH)** per ECM 1.7.4 + Appendix X required for modifications. Zone-specific.
    65→- **Restoration ratios (ECM 1.7.5):** Outside CWQZ (Zone 1): 2:1 / 3:1 / 4:1 for Poor / Fair / Good-or-Excellent condition (Good+ requires LUC variance). Inside CWQZ (Zone 2): 4:1 / 6:1 / 8:1 — all require LUC variance.
    66→- **Note re ECM cross-reference:** ECM § 1.7.1 still references the repealed § 25-8-364; current governing provision is LDC § 25-8-263.
    67→
    68→### Critical Water Quality Zone (CWQZ) — the buffer system
    69→
    70→- **Suburban watersheds — fixed buffer widths from centerline:** 100 ft (minor, 64–320 ac); 200 ft (intermediate, 320–640 ac); 300 ft (major, >640 ac). Buffer averaging permitted per ECM 1.5.2.D.
    71→- **CWQZ is largely undevelopable.** Most encroachments require an LUC variance under the enhanced § 25-8-41(B) standard (must prevent reasonable, economic use of the **entire** property).
    72→- Ponds, fill, retaining walls, parking, buildings, and spray irrigation are prohibited in CWQZ outright in most cases. Trails permitted at ≥50 ft from CEF edge under § 25-8-281(C)(3) without variance.
    73→- WQTZ is less restrictive but still constrains pond siting and stormwater controls.
    74→
    75→### Erosion Hazard Zone (EHZ)
    76→
    77→- EHZ analysis triggered when development is within 100 ft of a classified waterway centerline (≥64 acres drainage) or 200 ft of the Colorado River OHWM downstream of Longhorn Dam (LDC § 25-7-32(C)).
    78→- Seven-step DCM Appendix E procedure: meander belt delineation (if sinuosity ≥1.2), bankfull geometry, incision depth, side slope projections to 100 ft max (steep terrain) or 20 ft min setback from tops of bank.
    79→- WPD/ERM concurrence on protective works required.
    80→
    81→### Critical Environmental Features (CEFs)
    82→
    83→- 150-ft standard setback (LDC § 25-8-281). Reduction requires administrative variance under § 25-8-42(B)(5) only if all CEF characteristics can be preserved.
    84→- Point recharge features (caves, sinkholes) — admin variance minimum 50 ft, with 12 ECM 1.10.4.B conditions precluding further reduction.
    85→- Canyon rimrock / bluff admin variance unavailable on upslope grade ≥15% or average grade ≥10% — LUC variance required.
    86→- Cave footprint assumption: 300 ft from entrance when subsurface extent unmapped (ECM 1.10.3.C).
    87→
    88→### Cut / fill grading limits
    89→
    90→- **4-ft standard limit** in non-urban watersheds (LDC §§ 25-8-341 / 25-8-342); urban watersheds exempt.
    91→- **8-ft administrative variance maximum** in the Desired Development Zone (DDZ); ECM 1.3.3 form. Unavailable on slopes >15% or within 100 ft of a classified waterway, or anywhere in the Drinking Water Protection Zone (DWPZ — Barton Springs Zone, Barton Creek watershed, all water supply rural and suburban watersheds), except for public primary/secondary educational facilities.
    92→- **>8 ft cut/fill** anywhere, or **any** cut/fill above 4 ft in DWPZ: LUC variance under § 25-8-41 required.
    93→- **Cover sheet citation watch:** flag any reference to "§ 25-8-42(B)(6)" — that subsection was renumbered to (B)(7) by Ord. No. 20221027-045 (effective 2022-11-07).
    94→
    95→### Watershed impervious cover limits
    96→
    97→- **Urban IC:** set by zoning code (LDC § 25-2-492); gross site area; no Q-1/Q-2 tables.
    98→- **Suburban IC:** 45–80% gross site area depending on use type and whether transfer of development intensity is used (LDC § 25-8-392).
    99→- **Barton Springs Zone IC:** 15% over EARZ/recharge; 20% Barton Creek contributing zone; 25% remainder of BSZ contributing zone (net site area; LDC § 25-8-514). **No variance available — Save Our Springs (Article 13).**
   100→- **Interbasin diversion threshold:** lesser of 20% of gross site area or 1 acre (LDC § 25-8-365). Above this, admin variance via § 25-8-42(B)(9) or LUC variance.
   101→
   102→### Drainage easement
   103→
   104→- Regulatory 100-yr floodplain must be **entirely contained** within a drainage easement on the plat. Easement dedication variances available at LDC § 25-7-152(E) for full-purpose city limits only.
   105→
   106→## Opportunities to evaluate
   107→
   108→- **Redevelopment Exception (LDC §§ 25-8-25 / -26 / -27).** Existing developed sites in Urban or Suburban watersheds may retain existing impervious cover that exceeds current limits. Substantive eligibility requires water quality treatment for the full 0.5" / 1.0" capture and other procedural conditions. Often decisive for infill projects.
   109→- **CLOMR / LOMR.** Where the FEMA boundary is conservative relative to actual topography, a no-rise modification + LOMR can remove parts of the parcel from SFHA, unlocking buildable area. Budget 6–12 months for FEMA review and stage CLOMC acknowledgment before site plan permit.
   110→- **Compensatory storage / fill in 100-yr (non-floodway).** Cut/fill to raise pad elevation can work in the 100-yr floodplain (outside the floodway) with proper no-rise + volume compensation + 2-ft freeboard. Not available in floodway.
   111→- **Buffer averaging in CWQZ (ECM 1.5.2.D).** Suburban watersheds allow buffer width averaging so long as total area is preserved — can free up usable land while still meeting CWQZ obligations.
   112→- **Atlas 14 watershed amendment status.** Watersheds not yet updated to Atlas 14 may still produce smaller COA boundaries than updated neighbors. Verify status; the boundary you map at concept may grow before site plan.
   113→- **Conservation easements / parkland dedication.** Floodplain-encumbered area unsuitable for development can satisfy parkland dedication or conservation easement obligations, potentially yielding fee credits.
   114→- **Public-facility cut/fill pathway.** Public primary/secondary educational facilities have a unique exemption to the DWPZ ban on cut/fill admin variances (AISD Interlocal Agreement § 10.2.4.1 / LDC § 25-2-835).
   115→- **TIRZ / Waller Creek tunnel exception.** Sites discharging directly to Lady Bird Lake, Lake Travis, Lake Austin, the Colorado River, or Waller Creek below the tunnel inlet within the TIRZ are exempt from no-increased-peak-flow-rate requirements (DCM 1.2.2.F).
   116→- **ECM 1.7.3 floodplain-modification exemptions** from restoration ratios: (A) public health/safety necessity (with WPD Director letter); (B) significant demonstrable environmental benefit; (C) conditionally-allowed CWQZ development. Useful when restoration ratios would otherwise make a project infeasible.
   117→
   118→## Inputs needed from Phase 2
   119→
   120→- **environmental.md** — FEMA flood zone determination, FIRM panel number + effective date, COA fully-developed floodplain extent, CWQZ / WQTZ / EHZ overlay results, classified waterway proximity, EARZ status, Barton Springs Zone status, CEF inventory from ERI or GIS, watershed classification (Urban / Suburban / Water Supply Suburban / Water Supply Rural / Barton Springs Zone), Atlas 14 amendment status for the watershed.
   121→- **property-records.md** — recorded drainage easements, plat conditions referencing flood/drainage, prior CLOMR/LOMR letters, prior environmental or floodplain variance approvals (check expiration under LDC § 25-1-217 — variances expire 1 year after effective date unless associated with an approved plan).
   122→- **phase1-extraction/concept-plan-data.md** — proposed grading depths, building footprint relative to mapped floodplain boundaries, proposed FFE, pond locations (water quality + detention), driveway/parking layout relative to CWQZ and EHZ, proposed disturbance area relative to CEF buffers.
   123→- **adjacent-context.md** — upstream/downstream conditions for no-adverse-impact framing; nearby preliminary FIRMs in process.
   124→
   125→## Output structure
   126→
   127→Standard discipline output shape. See `references/phase3-disciplines.md`.
   128→
   129→## Severity heuristics
   130→
   131→| Finding | Severity |
   132→|---|---|
   133→| Building footprint or parking within COA 25-yr floodplain (floodway) | `significant` — 0.00-ft rise required; Council variance unavailable if any rise results |
   134→| Project in Barton Springs Zone exceeding 15% IC (or 20% / 25% per sub-zone) | `significant` — SOS Article 13, no variance available |
   135→| Building footprint within FEMA SFHA + COA 100-yr, freeboard + compensatory storage achievable | `moderate` |
   136→| Building or parking within FEMA SFHA but outside COA fully-developed boundary, freeboard achievable | `moderate` — § 25-7-93 exception pathway likely |
   137→| COA fully-developed 100-yr floodplain materially larger than FEMA SFHA, encroaches on developable area | `moderate` to `significant` depending on coverage |
   138→| Site within 100 ft of classified waterway centerline, cut/fill needed >4 ft | `moderate` — administrative variance unavailable; LUC variance required |
   139→| CWQZ encroachment proposed for parking, pond, or building | `significant` — enhanced § 25-8-41(B) standard (must prevent reasonable economic use of entire property) |
   140→| EHZ overlaps proposed disturbance | `moderate` — analysis required; protective works concurrence with WPD/ERM |
   141→| CEF setback reduction needed for non-wetland CEF | `moderate` — admin variance pathway via ECM 1.3.3 |
   142→| Cut/fill 4–8 ft in DDZ, slopes <15%, >100 ft from classified waterway | `moderate` — admin variance available |
   143→| Cut/fill >8 ft anywhere, or cut/fill in DWPZ | `significant` — LUC variance only; not available in BSZ for cut/fill on slopes >15% |
   144→| Watershed has pending preliminary FIRM (effective FIRM in transition) | `moderate` — boundary may grow before site plan; design to preliminary |
   145→| Floodplain study not yet performed for ≥64-acre waterway on or adjacent to site | `moderate` — Phase 3 cannot finalize FP boundary without it |
   146→| Parcel entirely outside FEMA SFHA, COA 100-yr, CWQZ, EHZ, and CEF buffers | `note` |
   147→| LOMA / LOMR pathway available for portion of parcel | `opportunity` |
   148→| Redevelopment Exception eligibility for IC | `opportunity` |
   149→| Buffer averaging in CWQZ unlocks developable area while preserving total buffer | `opportunity` |
   150→| TIRZ / Waller Creek tunnel discharge exception applies | `opportunity` |
   151→
   152→## Common pitfalls
   153→
   154→- **Citing only FEMA SFHA.** The COA fully-developed floodplain is broader in Atlas 14 watersheds — design only to FEMA and you will land in COA-floodplain encroachment at site plan review.
   155→- **Treating COA 25-yr as a "minor" boundary.** The COA 25-yr floodplain **is** the COA floodway. 0.00-ft rise is required; Council cannot grant variance if any rise results. It is the hardest line on the map.
   156→- **Re-delineating FEMA boundary to onsite topo.** FEMA must be copied directly from the FIRM panel shapefile. Re-delineating is a deficiency signature.
   157→- **COA boundary matching FEMA exactly.** Indicates the engineer used FEMA data rather than the City's regulatory hydraulic model — also a violation signature.
   158→- **Stale code citations.** Cover sheet referencing "§ 25-8-42(B)(6)" for cut/fill admin variance (renumbered to (B)(7) in 2022); plans or variance letters citing repealed §§ 25-8-691 through 25-8-696 for notification requirements (repealed 2022-11-07); ECM § 1.7.1 cross-reference to repealed § 25-8-364 (now § 25-8-263).
   159→- **Assuming compensatory storage anywhere.** Volume compensation works for fill in the 100-yr floodplain outside the floodway; it does **not** create a pathway through the floodway.
   160→- **Conflating EHZ with CWQZ.** Different boundaries, different rules. The EHZ may extend beyond the CWQZ in steep terrain (up to 100-ft setback) or be contained within it.
   161→- **Missing the 64-acre threshold.** Below 64 acres of contributing drainage area, no COA floodplain is required to be delineated — but if City or FEMA has already mapped one, it still applies.
   162→- **Missing the Atlas 14 watershed status check.** Watersheds updated post-2019-11-25 require Atlas 14 rainfall (Rule R161-20.01); older models in non-updated watersheds will be rejected for new floodplain studies.
   163→- **Assuming variance pathways exist in the Barton Springs Zone.** Save Our Springs (Article 13) cannot be varied — not by admin variance, not by LUC variance, not by Council.
   164→- **Variance expiration.** Variances expire 1 year after effective date (LDC § 25-1-217) unless a plan/permit application was timely filed. Old approval letters on a parcel may already be void.
   165→- **Drainage easement scope.** The regulatory 100-yr floodplain must be **entirely contained** within a drainage easement on the plat — a partial easement is a deficiency.
   166→- **CLOMC timing.** FEMA CLOMC acknowledgment letter must be in the project file **before** preliminary plan or site plan permit issues — not after. Budget 6–12 months.
   167→- **PE no-rise certification format.** Floodway no-rise must be a **separate** PE-sealed letter (LDC § 25-12-54(D)(11)), not implied by the WSE comparison table.
   168→- **ASCE 24-14 letters.** One per structure type in the floodplain — bridges, culverts, retaining walls, structural fill, piers, fencing, buildings. A single combined letter is a common deficiency.

# Floodplain Findings --- 12713 Cinchring Ln

**Property:** 12713 Cinchring Ln, Austin, TX 78727 --- Lot 12, Block M, Scofield Subdivision
**Proposed use:** Demolish existing SFR; build ground-up duplex (2 units)
**Lot:** ~7,840 sq ft (0.18 acres), SF-2 zoning
**Watershed:** Walnut Creek (Suburban)
**Date:** 2026-06-03

---

## Summary

- **No floodplain encumbrance.** The property is in FEMA Zone X (FIRM Panel 48453C0115E, effective 06/16/1993), outside both the 100-year and 500-year floodplain. The survey confirms this determination. No floodplain development permit, elevation certificate, CLOMR/LOMR, or ASCE 24 certification is required.
- **No CWQZ, EHZ, or CEF constraints identified.** The lot is an upland site at approximately 850--870 ft elevation, well above the Walnut Creek floodplain corridor. No classified waterway is on or immediately adjacent to the parcel, and no Critical Water Quality Zone, Erosion Hazard Zone, or Critical Environmental Feature buffers encroach on the site.
- **No floodway (COA 25-yr) or COA fully-developed 100-yr floodplain impact.** The upland position places the site outside both the FEMA SFHA and the City of Austin's fully-developed-conditions floodplain, which can be broader than FEMA in Atlas 14-updated watersheds. Neither boundary reaches this lot.
- **No drainage easement encumbrance for floodplain purposes.** The recorded easements (5-ft PUE, blanket electrical easement, ingress/egress utility easement) are utility-related; no drainage easement is recorded on the plat, and none is required because the regulatory 100-yr floodplain does not cross the parcel.
- **This discipline presents no material constraint to the proposed duplex development.** The floodplain assessment is complete and favorable. Remaining environmental obligations (impervious cover, water quality controls, tree survey, BCCP fee) are addressed in the Environmental Landscape and Site Drainage disciplines.

---

## Findings

### 1. FEMA Flood Zone Determination

- **Severity:** note
- **Citation:** FEMA FIRM Panel 48453C0115E, effective 06/16/1993; property survey; DCM 1.2.6.B
- **Finding:** The property is mapped in FEMA Zone X --- areas determined to be outside both the 1% annual chance (100-year) and 0.2% annual chance (500-year) floodplains. The survey explicitly states the property does not lie within the 100-year flood prone area. Zone X designation means no Special Flood Hazard Area (SFHA) applies.
- **Implication for the developer:** No FEMA-related floodplain obligations attach to this site. No flood insurance purchase requirement under NFIP. No elevation certificate, floodplain development permit, or FEMA map amendment (CLOMR/LOMR) is needed. No ASCE 24-14 structural compliance is required.
- **Recommended next step:** None. Retain the FIRM panel citation and survey flood zone note in the project file for the building permit application.

### 2. City of Austin Fully-Developed 100-Year Floodplain

- **Severity:** note
- **Citation:** LDC Ch. 25-7; LDC Ch. 25-12; DCM 1.2.6.A-B; Rule R161-20.01 (Atlas 14)
- **Finding:** The COA fully-developed 100-year floodplain, derived from City regulatory hydraulic models with Atlas 14 rainfall data (where applicable), does not extend to this upland lot. The Walnut Creek floodplain corridor lies at materially lower elevations. This is consistent with the site's 850--870 ft elevation and its position within a fully built-out subdivision on higher ground. No COA floodplain boundary encroaches on the parcel.
- **Implication for the developer:** No COA floodplain development permit is required. No compensatory storage, no-rise analysis, or freeboard calculations are needed. The project is not subject to the COA 25-year floodway zero-rise standard (LDC 25-12-54).
- **Recommended next step:** Confirm the COA GIS floodplain layer at site plan submission as a procedural step. No engineering analysis required.

### 3. CWQZ / WQTZ Applicability

- **Severity:** note
- **Citation:** LDC 25-8-261; ECM 1.5.2; DCM 1.2.6.A.1 (64-acre classified waterway threshold)
- **Finding:** Critical Water Quality Zone buffers in Suburban watersheds apply to classified waterways with 64 or more acres of contributing drainage area. No such waterway is on or immediately adjacent to this lot. The lot is an interior subdivision parcel surrounded by other residential lots and local streets, with no surface water feature or classified drainage channel present. The CWQZ does not encroach on the site.
- **Implication for the developer:** No CWQZ use restrictions apply. No buffer averaging analysis or LUC variance under the enhanced LDC 25-8-41(B) standard is needed. Proposed building and impervious cover placement is unconstrained by CWQZ.
- **Recommended next step:** None.

### 4. Erosion Hazard Zone (EHZ) Applicability

- **Severity:** note
- **Citation:** LDC 25-7-32(C); DCM Appendix E
- **Finding:** EHZ analysis is triggered when development is within 100 ft of a classified waterway centerline (64 or more acres drainage area). No classified waterway is within 100 ft of this lot. No EHZ has been identified or is expected.
- **Implication for the developer:** No EHZ setback analysis, meander belt delineation, or WPD/ERM concurrence on protective works is required.
- **Recommended next step:** None.

### 5. Critical Environmental Features (CEFs)

- **Severity:** note
- **Citation:** LDC 25-8-281; ECM 1.10.0; City of Austin Watershed Protection karst database
- **Finding:** No known CEFs (springs, caves, sinkholes, point recharge features, rimrock, bluffs) have been identified at or immediately adjacent to the site. The Scofield subdivision in north Austin is developed on Cretaceous-age formations not typically associated with significant karst features. The Edwards Aquifer Recharge Zone is well south of this property.
- **Implication for the developer:** No 150-ft CEF protective buffer applies. No administrative or LUC variance for CEF setback reduction is needed.
- **Recommended next step:** The Environmental Resource Inventory (ERI) form, required at site plan application, will provide formal City confirmation of CEF status. This is a procedural requirement, not a risk item.

### 6. FIRM Panel Age

- **Severity:** note
- **Citation:** FIRM Panel 48453C0115E, effective 06/16/1993
- **Finding:** The effective FIRM panel dates to 1993. While older panels can sometimes be superseded by preliminary FIRMs from watershed restudies, a Zone X determination on an upland lot at 850--870 ft elevation is extremely unlikely to be affected by any FEMA restudy of the Walnut Creek watershed. No pending preliminary FIRM affecting this panel has been identified.
- **Implication for the developer:** The 1993 effective date does not create risk for this parcel. The Zone X designation is stable.
- **Recommended next step:** As a best practice, confirm at permit application that no preliminary FIRM has been published for this panel. This is low-effort and low-risk.

### 7. Drainage Easement Status

- **Severity:** note
- **Citation:** LDC 25-7-152; plat records (Cabinet 91, Slide 264-265)
- **Finding:** The recorded easements on this lot (5-ft PUE, blanket electrical easement, ingress/egress utility easement) are utility-related. No drainage easement is recorded, and none is required because the regulatory 100-year floodplain does not cross the parcel. The drainage easement dedication requirement (LDC 25-7-152) applies only where the regulatory floodplain exists on a lot.
- **Implication for the developer:** No drainage easement dedication or variance is needed.
- **Recommended next step:** None.

---

## Open Questions for the Engineer

1. **Atlas 14 watershed amendment status for Walnut Creek:** Has the Walnut Creek watershed been updated to Atlas 14 rainfall per Rule R161-20.01 (effective 2019-11-25)? This does not affect the floodplain determination for this upland lot, but should be documented for completeness and in case any drainage study is required for site plan review.

2. **Preliminary FIRM check:** Has FEMA published any preliminary FIRM panels for the Walnut Creek watershed that would supersede Panel 48453C0115E? Again, unlikely to affect a Zone X upland lot, but confirm for the file.

3. **Contributing drainage area to the lot:** Does any concentrated flow path with 64 or more acres of contributing drainage area cross or abut the lot? The answer is almost certainly no given the interior subdivision location, but the engineer should confirm this at the site plan stage per DCM 1.2.6.A.1.
